title: Usability Testing
description: Plan, run, and analyse usability tests. Tests test plan writing, result synthesis, and remote testing strategy.

seo.overviewBody: Usability testing validates whether real users can accomplish tasks efficiently in an interface. UX leads assess designers on creating unmoderated/moderated usability test plans, measuring task completion rates, logging user errors, and calculating System Usability Scale (SUS) scores.

deliverables.title: 1. Usability Test Protocol & Task Scenarios Document
deliverables.desc: Testing plan outlining realistic user task scenarios, success criteria, and post-task questionnaire scripts.

deliverables.title: 2. Video Session Observation & Error Log
deliverables.desc: Session log documenting user task completion rates, time-on-task metrics, misclicks, and verbalized frustrations.

deliverables.title: 3. System Usability Scale (SUS) Benchmark Report
deliverables.desc: Quantitative report computing SUS survey scores (0-100) and outlining UX remediation priorities.

faqs.question: How is the System Usability Scale (SUS) score calculated?
faqs.answer: SUS uses a 10-item Likert scale survey. Individual item scores (0-4) are summed and multiplied by 2.5 to yield a normalized usability benchmark score from 0 to 100.

faqs.question: What is an acceptable System Usability Scale (SUS) benchmark score?
faqs.answer: An SUS score above 68 is considered average; scores above 80 indicate excellent usability.

faqs.question: What is the difference between moderated and unmoderated usability testing?
faqs.answer: Moderated testing has a live facilitator guiding the participant in real time. Unmoderated testing allows users to complete tasks independently via automated platforms (like Maze or UserTesting).
